title: DDIAS shields single-stranded DNA in mitosis and promotes vertebrate brain development
title_zh: DDIAS 在有丝分裂中保护单链 DNA 并促进脊椎动物大脑发育
abstract: DNA double-strand breaks and unresolved DNA replication intermediates are particularly dangerous during mitosis. Paradoxically, cells inactivate canonical DNA repair mechanisms during chromosome segregation in favor of alternative pathways that depend on TOPBP1 and CIP2A, but how these pathways function is still poorly defined. Here, we describe the identification of DDIAS as a mitosis-specific DNA damage response protein. We establish DDIAS as a phosphorylation-dependent component and effector of the TOPBP1-CIP2A complex, and we demonstrate that DDIAS protects single-stranded DNA from aberrant nucleolytic processing to safeguard chromosome integrity during mitosis, particularly in BRCA1-/BRCA2-deficient cells. We also identify biallelic inactivating mutations in DDIAS in patients with a severe neurodevelopmental disorder and, using human cerebral organoids and zebrafish, we show that DDIAS plays a critical and evolutionarily conserved role in limiting DNA damage specifically in neural progenitor cells. These findings demonstrate a physiological role for the DNA damage response in mitosis during vertebrate neurodevelopment.
abstract_zh: DNA 双链断裂和未解决的 DNA 复制中间体在有丝分裂期间尤为危险。矛盾的是，细胞在染色体分离期间关闭传统 DNA 修复机制，转而依赖 TOPBP1 和 CIP2A 的替代通路，但这些通路的具体功能尚不清楚。本文描述了 DDIAS 作为有丝分裂特异性 DNA 损伤应答蛋白的鉴定。我们确立了 DDIAS 作为 TOPBP1-CIP2A 复合物的磷酸化依赖性组分和效应子，并证明 DDIAS 通过防止异常核酸酶处理来保护单链 DNA，维护有丝分裂期间染色体完整性，尤其是在 BRCA1-/BRCA2 缺失细胞中。我们还在严重神经发育障碍患者中鉴定了 DDIAS 的双等位体失活突变，并利用人类大脑类器官和斑马鱼模型表明 DDIAS 在限制神经祖细胞中特异性 DNA 损伤方面发挥关键且进化保守的作用。这些发现展示了 DNA 损伤应答在有丝分裂期间对脊椎动物神经发育的生理作用。
